definition: The departure came from what arrived: not enough, or it did not add up. Acted on by whoever owns intake.
The departure came from the rules themselves. Acted on by whoever owns the policy.
A person assessed risk or consequence. Acted on through training and calibration.
Money, people, time or a deadline shaped it. Acted on through funding and scheduling.
Decided by someone outside the organisation. Managed rather than fixed.
Beyond the decider delegation. Acted on by whoever sets delegations.
A departure that does not fit the defined loci.
